title: Record Migrant Surge Overwhelms Spain's Ceuta Enclave, Triggering EU Crisis Response
detail: An estimated 50,000-60,000 migrants crossed from Morocco into Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta (population 84,000) over three days, the largest single mass-crossing event in the territory's history; at least 72 people died attempting the crossing. Spanish PM Pedro Sánchez blamed trafficking networks that spread false claims online — based on a misreading of a Spanish Supreme Court ruling on sea-arrival returns — that migrants who reached Ceuta could travel onward to mainland Spain and the rest of the EU. Twenty-two EU heads of state and government wrote to EU leaders requesting an emergency meeting to address what they called 'uncontrolled mass crossings' and the 'instrumentalization of migration'. Spain temporarily reimposed border checks on travellers arriving from Italy after Rome refused to lift checks it had imposed on arrivals from Spain, deepening intra-EU tension over free movement.
